title: Lehi in the valley of Lemuel
summary: Nephi recounts that his father, Lehi, saw, heard, and spoke these things and many more while dwelling in a tent in the valley of Lemuel.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi dwelt in a tent in the valley of Lemuel.
Lehi saw, heard, and spoke these things and a great many more that could not be written upon the plates.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi may be shown at a tent in the valley of Lemuel.
unspecified_visual_details: Lehi’s appearance and the tent’s appearance are unspecified.
The content of what Lehi saw, heard, and spoke is unspecified.

narration.text: And all these things did my father see, and hear, and speak, as he dwelt in a tent, in the valley of Lemuel

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The first-person narrator is Nephi; “my father” refers to Lehi.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific visions, sounds, or conversations whose content is not supplied.
Do not identify Lehi as the father of Lehi.

title: Nephi explains the plates
summary: Nephi distinguishes these plates from those on which he makes a full account of his people, and explains the commanded purpose of each set.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the plates on which he makes a full account of his people are named Nephi after himself, and both sets are called the plates of Nephi.
Nephi says he received a commandment of the Lord to make these plates so an account of his people’s ministry would be engraved.
The other plates were to record the reign of kings, wars, and contentions; these plates were mostly for ministry, and the other plates mostly for those subjects.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown explaining the distinction between the two sets of plates.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance and surroundings; the plates’ material, size, and appearance.

narration.text: these plates also are called the plates of Nephi.
Nevertheless, I have received a commandment of the Lord
for the special purpose that there should be an account engraven of the ministry of my people.
these plates are for the more part of the ministry

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses explain the plates’ purposes; they do not narrate engraving as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or giving the commandment as a present scene.
Do not portray the plates being engraved as a narrated event.

title: A purpose known to the Lord
summary: Nephi says the Lord commanded him to make the plates for a wise purpose he does not know. He states that the Lord knows all things from the beginning and prepares a way to accomplish his works among the children of men, having power to fulfill all his words.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commanded Nephi to make the plates for a wise purpose in him, which purpose Nephi does not know.
Nephi states that the Lord knows all things from the beginning, prepares a way to accomplish all his works among the children of men, and has power to fulfill all his words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown as the narrator; the text specifies no particular action.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, posture, surroundings, and whether the plates are visible.

narration.text: Wherefore, the Lord hath commanded me to make these plates for a wise purpose in him, which purpose I know not.
But the Lord knoweth all things from the beginning;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's knowledge, preparation, and power are statements of teaching, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or portray the figurative way as a visible event.
